discussion_comments.comment_body:
Cache is FIFO, not LRU (`Map.keys()` returns keys [in insertion order](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Map/keys), `.set()` does not re-insert).

I haven't tested if FIFO is faster, but my assumption from testing is that this only gets stressed during resize events.
I think the cache size can be quite a bit bigger actually.
I'll test with a 200-length multilingual conversation with varying cache sizes. I don't even know if it's getting populated.

discussion_comments.comment_body: I don't think there's a need to save the cache to disk. Per process, we only have a single session (which is also full in memory, see session-manager.ts. The cached summary (and there should be really only ever one cached summary) is miniscule in comparison to that. Saving it out to disk is unnecessary. That we'll have an empty cache when resuming a session is not a big deal, as after the first agent turn, the bg summary will be created anyways (iiuc)
